planned_path.path_summary: Use the full authorized wage-gain table to regress individual log wage gain on education groups, estimating the no-high-school versus college-degree contrast while adjusting for country, sex, age at last home job, and job timing.

path_signature.sample_restriction: Authorized dataset rows with nonmissing required variables and positive adjusted wages.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required columns and constructed variables; drop nonpositive adjusted wages for log transformation.
path_signature.variable_construction: Compute log wage gain, education groups, and age at last home job; no aggregation.
path_signature.inference_rule: A positive no_high_school coefficient relative to college_degree is support; p < 0.05 indicates strong statistical evidence and p >= 0.05 with a positive estimate is weak directional support. A negative estimate is inconclusive unless affirmative contrary evidence is established.
path_signature.estimand_quantity: Adjusted coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree in individual log wage gain.
path_signature.outcome_scale: Log wage-gain units and exponentiated percent difference.
path_signature.contrast: edyrs <= 8 versus edyrs >= 16, with intermediate schooling categories retained in the model.
path_signature.target_population: Immigrants in the authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx sample with positive adjusted home and U.S. wages and nonmissing model variables.
path_signature.time_scope: Last home-country job to last U.S. job.

deviations.candidate_choice: Adjusted OLS with country, sex, age_home_job, age_home_job squared, yearLastHomeJob, and yearLastUsJob controls.
deviations.justification: Task1 has no restrictions, and these are verified demographic, country, and timing variables relevant to wage comparisons. Sector and region controls are not introduced.

execution_result.status_reason: The agent followed the planned Task1 path exactly: it used the authorized wage-gain table, constructed log wage gain and education categories as planned, and estimated the adjusted OLS model with HC1 robust standard errors. No implementation repairs were made.

planned_path.path_summary: Use the supplied pooled poor-country wage-gain table, retain Mexico, and estimate the no-high-school versus college-degree difference in log wage gains without sector or region controls.

path_signature.sample_restriction: Use the authorized pooled poor-country table and retain Mexico; no additional country restriction is possible because the file has no GDP-per-worker variable or source indicator.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required variables and constructed variables; drop nonpositive adjusted wages for log transformation.
path_signature.variable_construction: Compute log wage gain and education groups; no controls, aggregation, sector adjustment, or region adjustment.
path_signature.inference_rule: A positive no_high_school coefficient relative to college_degree is support; p < 0.05 indicates strong statistical evidence and p >= 0.05 with a positive estimate is weak directional support. A negative estimate is inconclusive unless affirmative contrary evidence is established.
path_signature.estimand_quantity: Unadjusted coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree in individual log wage gain.
path_signature.outcome_scale: Log wage-gain units and exponentiated percent difference.
path_signature.contrast: edyrs <= 8 versus edyrs >= 16, with intermediate schooling categories retained in the model.
path_signature.target_population: Authorized pooled poor-country NIS/Migration Projects wage-gain sample including Mexico, with positive adjusted wages and nonmissing education.
path_signature.time_scope: Last home-country job to last U.S. job.

execution_result.status_reason: The agent followed the planned Task2 path exactly: it used the pooled authorized wage-gain table, retained Mexico, constructed log wage gain and education categories, and estimated the unadjusted OLS model without sector or region controls. No implementation repairs were made.
